found_by: the CI fuzz smoke job (fuzz-macos), read-write mode, third run: AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free
base: a read-write mutant of a 4 MiB seed, the runner's own artifact, trimmed by the one trailing byte the fuzzer had appended: the in-process harness takes any length, ext4dump refuses a device that is not a multiple of 512 before any script runs

edits.what: corruption that makes a create fail after its transaction has dirtied a group descriptor block
edits.note: the exact bytes are the fuzzer's; the property that matters is a create that aborts with a block record kept alive by an older transaction's queued buffers

symptom: The aborted transaction was freed with a still-needed block record linked into its list and pointing at it. The next create dirtied the same block, found the record in the journal's tree, and jbd_trans_change_ownership's LIST_REMOVE wrote into the freed transaction: heap-use-after-free at ext4_journal.c:2556, reached from ext4_fs_put_block_group_ref via ext4_ialloc_alloc_inode.
fixed_by: patch 0075 -- a record that outlives its owner is unlinked and orphaned; ownership change unlinks only an owned record
reproduce: EXT4_FUZZ_MODE=rw build/bin/ext4_fuzz -runs=1 (or the hostile suite under make test-asan)
note_on_detection: A use-after-free: faults only under AddressSanitizer, like fixtures 0001, 0004 and 0012.
